eyebrow: SQL for Oracle Financials · Chapter Three
subtitle: Lesson 11 · Aggregation and Aging

caption: No GROUP BY means exactly one row back — a grand total.

code:
SELECT vendor_id,
       SUM(invoice_amount) AS total_invoiced,
       COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
FROM ap_invoices_all
GROUP BY vendor_id;
caption: One result row per distinct vendor_id.

code:
-- ERROR: invoice_num isn't aggregated and isn't in GROUP BY
SELECT vendor_id, invoice_num, SUM(invoice_amount)
FROM ap_invoices_all
GROUP BY vendor_id;
caption: Every non-aggregated SELECT column must appear in GROUP BY.

code:
SELECT i.invoice_num, SUM(ip.amount) AS total_paid
FROM ap_invoices_all i
INNER JOIN ap_invoice_payments_all ip
    ON ip.invoice_id = i.invoice_id
GROUP BY i.invoice_num;
caption: Lesson 7's multi-row-per-invoice join, folded back to one row per invoice.

subtitle: Filtering on the aggregated total itself, not the raw rows.
